title: Junk hill @ busy Junction
description:
It is said that Bannerghatta road is one of the fast-developing roads in all of Bangalore. But the photos attached to this complaint says otherwise. Don't believe it? The spot marked on the map and the photos explaining the scene is less than 10meters from the very famous Vega City mall. In spite of being one of the busiest roads with a lot of traffic. People usually swim through this heap of garbage to cross the Jedi Mara signal. I commute every day to my office using the same road having to see such blissful sight every day of my life. I have also seen people living nearby or just on the opposite side of the road throw food/plastic/wet/dry/degradable/non-degradable wastes and create such a beautiful mystery making it hard to classify the type of waste. But enough of all the jokes and sarcasm, let's get serious for a minute. I hope the below point will give a gist of the problem. 
1. I have witnessed a 2-wheeler rider fell and got badly hurt as he got out of balance when his vehicle moved over some wet waste. 
2. This is the welcome mat for people getting down from the BTMC buses. 
3. Because of this people are not able to use footpath and are compelled to get on the road to cross the street. And even when crossing one must take a deep breath so that your olfactory nodes don't get damaged. 
4. Since this occupies half of the road, commuters can use only the other half of the road. Many a time this causes serious traffic blockage. 
5. And since this is the heart of the rainy season all the dumped garbage gets clog the drainpipes and causes rainwater to overflow on the streets. 
Taking all these points into consideration, I request the concerned team/authority to take necessary actions and solve this issue. And I also ask to impose strict rules and heavy penality for irresponsible behaviors. Thanks in advance.

title: Outer ring road is swept but the mud/sand etc is not picked up, instead left in mounds, along the roads, medians , on footpaths etc
description:
2 months back, i took a ride from Bellandur to Kalyan Nagar and back( I live in Bangalore ) with the specific intention of taking pictures along the outer ring road to capture the negligence of the authorities who are in charge of cleaning the roads in this stretch. In short here is what you see:
1) Mounds of sand/mud along the sides or medians of the ORR in many stretches including flyovers, maximum after the More flyover when going towards KR Puram station. These mounds are not natural formations, they have been made by someone, quite obvious by the people who have swept the road, perhaps with the intention that it would be picked up by another team , but then that has not happened. These mounds of mud still exist in after a month!
2) You can see the same mounds of mud and sand on the top portion of flyover to Kasturinagar from Tin Factory. The mud and sand are neatly arranged as small mountains( kids might love to see them !! ) on the footpath. Again they exist till date!!
3) The state of underpasses at the center of the underpass right under the bridge on top, should be seen, mainly the Ram Murthy Nagar and Horamavu underpass. You can see lot of sand/mud on the side of the road along with lot of the same accumulated on the footpaths. If a two wheeler goes towards the side of the roads in speed, the rider is sure of getting the "last ride".
I can go on and on listing such stuff. The same scenes can be seen on Indiranagar 100 ft road, sarjapur road, old airport road etc. I fail to understand this!! When someone has swept the road, am sure some money would have paid for doing the same, why is the stuff not being picked up!! Instead it is left lying there, in fact you can see plants growing in many of these sand/mud mounds!!
Can't Bangalore have cleaner roads, is it that difficult? Many a times citizens add to the mess by throwing garbage on top of these mounds of sand/mud. Please stop doing this!!
I have not seen this state in any other city.
The idea of taking the pics was that reaches the concerned authorities and they take some action. Now, just uploading the photos( around 50 of them ) would have been very boring. So, i decided to make a video with the photos, along with an inspirational song.
It is more than 2 months now but absolutely nothing has been done till now.

title: Huge traffic jams due to AET Junction bottleneck
description:
From past 6 months, traffic has worsened on Sarjapura road near Doddakannelli stretch during peak office hours due to bottleneck at AET Junction. Unfortunately, there is no alternative roads towards Marathahalli  apart from just outer ring road and Doddakannelli-Kadubesnahalli Road. Hence, all the traffic on Sarjapura road is distributed on both the streches and causing huge pile up of traffic on this road. The road is unscientific as it is does not have uniform consistent width. To add to woes, there is no lane discipline and which makes narrow width stretches as bottle necks before the junction.

Most of the times these days, it takes about 45 mins to 1 hour to just cross the AET junction from Andhra Bank, Doddakannelli (~2 KMs of stretch). Due to this , there is a huge loss in fuel and precious time.

As a short term solution, I believe BBMP and Bangalore traffic police should think of alternatives to de congest the AET junction and should think of laying parallel roads to outer ring road as a long term solution. However, it is upto agencies to think of best solution for benefit of citizens and city.

I wanted to know if there is any action plan in place by BBMP, Government of Karnataka and Bangalore City Police to provide a near term and long term solution.

title: Suggestion for Clean Bangalore
description:
There are many vacant sites in our Layout and also in entire BBMP limits. The owners of this sites are not at all taking care or visit these sites. Many sites are turned into dump yards and senseless people are throwing plastic waste/all type of garbage on these sites and garbage dumps are formed on many sites. A lot of unwanted bushes and vegetation grown on these sites are not cleaned which gives scope for snakes and rodents to make their home. Some sites are being used for illegal activities at nights. Vacant Site owners are not bothered. Problem is only for those who have constructed homes in between and residing there.
I request you to forward my following suggestion to concerned higher authorities, which will resolve the vacant site menace and also create revenue for BBMP and make Bangalore clean.
Most of these sites are purchased for investment purpose and those owners are comfortably staying in nice homes in other parts of Bengaluru. If any person who is already possessing a home or having a site in his name or in the name of his spouse in BBMP limits, and if he has any vacant site in Bengaluru, then a time limit of say 1 or 2 years to be given for any construction activity on that vacant site. If it is not done, then as a penalty, BBMP or Govt can charge property tax at ten times the normal tax, and maintain such sites, neatly. Alternatively, by  amending the related laws, Govt can take over such sites by paying a compensation at the rate of purchase price plus indexation benefit. 
Land is a scarce commodity, and Govt can not allow anyone to hoard it. Land price is jacked up only due to hoarding. As many politicians are holding huge vacant land in BBMP limits,I am aware that my suggestion will not be looked into. But I believe that some sincere officials in BBMP apply their mind to above suggestion which is source of revenue to BBMP and make my Bengaluru neat and clean.

title: Vehicle Horn noise issue
description:
My Apartment is facing the road side (Borewell Road, Whitefield) and vehicle frequency in this road is very high. I do not have issues with the vehicle noise made due to the travelling however nightmare is when drivers start awful honking, and it goes throughout the days & nights.

I have considered my options, like sound proofing my rooms but then, Soundproofing would cut out ventilation completely and if I keep any window open, vehicle horn sound would be severe. Think about the situation when you have your old parents, new born child or kids how they deal with such pathetic drivers’ honking attitude.

Honking is undoubtedly a perennial issue in any city, commuters keep honking because traffic rules are not enforced. Here I am also requesting others to come up with new/innovative ideas to deal with this worst situation. 

Keeping the concept of “NO HORN” Zone only works for few literate drivers, i thought of few other best solutions to this problem described as below. My options may be harsh for others but effective at the same time and this is not the time when we should react politely.

1- Instruct to heavy vehicle (tankers/truck/bus) manufacture to develop and fix such horns which must not have continuous sound when long press, horn sound must be intermittent no matter how hard driver presses. I don’t believe in providing training to the drivers. Responsible authority – Traffic police and civic authorities 

2- Stop selling such horns in outside/grey market-- if any driver installs any high decibel horns, penalize heavily; ask the reference of the shop who is selling such cacophony, approach and seal immediately. If driver doesn’t provide right contact, again penalize him for hiding the correct facts. Responsible authority – Traffic police and civic authorities

3- This option is real solution, every apartment must have two live cameras (one facing left, another facing right, if needed more), capture the video of drivers, which can automatically connect and send the data to traffic police, traffic police will send challan online/offline to concern vehicle owners. 
More complaints, more challans more revenue to Traffic police 

To mitigate this problem, create history and benchmark to other states traffic police must do the rightful job. Success of this problem will be measured by less honking. Responsible authority – Traffic police and civic authorities

I will attach video also to make people realize how hell this problem is. I suggest to concern department – If above provided solutions are not acceptable to you then you consider your options to solve this problem but do not close my compliant until proper solution provided. If you don’t consider your options and closing my complaint then write a note that you don’t have solution for this problem and you don’t consider my options because of various reasons.

title: Miserable condition of Panathur-Belagere Road Railway Underpass
description:
Panathur, due to its proximity to Whitefield and Sarjapura, has seen rapid growth in the last 2 years and is now filled with commercial properties and apartment complexes. Sobha Dream Acres, a massive undertaking on the Panathur-Belagere Road, has 6500 flats. Prestige Lake View, another apartment complex, has around 4000 flats to its name. All told there should be more than 15000 flats. 
Being extremely narrow, this road can barely handle two-way traffic. It is filled with garbage and potholes and is perpetually being dug up on some pretext. The icing on the cake is a narrow railway vent at the end of this stretch which allows only one-way traffic to commute at a time. 
The menace on the Panathur-Belagere Road begins even before sunrise at times and continues for the rest of the day. Over 20,000 vehicles pass through this road daily where only one side is let to travel at a time. The presence of a large number of water tankers only adds to the chaos as these tanker drivers rush along with a complete disregard for traffic or rules. 
Making matters worse, the traffic on the Panathur-Belagere Road is not being managed by the city’s traffic police. This Herculean task falls to private security guards deployed by some IT companies.  Many people don’t conform to the guard’s instructions as they have no legal power to penalize anyone. 
The residents of Panathur have been waiting for years, in suspended animation, hoping to see a ray of light in what seems to be a never-ending tunnel of darkness.

title: Bad condition of footpaths
description:
Hello sir/madam,

Bangalore is a metropolitan city where so many people from different parts of India come to live here and work here. We work in companies in Bangalore for the welfare of the city. Everyone knows that bangalore is a city of great MNCs. So it's obvious that people want to come here to work. 

People work in bangalore which will benefit both government and to their self. Bangalore is a costly city, the cost of living here is so much compared to other cities but still people come to this city to make their livelihood. 

It's your responsibility to provide at least basic facilities to the people who came here far away from their house. And the basic thing is good condition of roads.

As there are so many companies in bangalore, there will be so many people around the office at a distance of 2-3 km. They may prefer to come by bus or by foot. Even if they take a bmtc bus, they still wants to walk a certain distance to reach a bus stop. But here the footpaths are in such a bad condition that it looks like a mud path rather than a footpath. Even with a light drizzle, the footpath becomes so dirty that people have to walk on the bricks side to the footpath. Then what is the use of having footpath if people are walking on the bricks?

I am working in a company in ITPL, whitefield. There is a footpath between brigade bhuwalka icon to international tech park and from international tech park to the den hotel. The path in between itpl and den is so bad. It's in the worst condition. That path is full of mud and there are no cement bricks on it. And whenever rain happens it will become a mini pond. There will be hundreds of people walking in that path everyday. As bangalore state government, it's your responsibility to take care of these footpaths. 

If you are not able to make a full path of cement bricks, atleast make a row of those so that people can walk on it in a line. 

Please I request you to take care of these paths. Because of that mud, we are suffering so much. I again request you to please take care of these roads. I am not asking you to give us money or jewellery, nor we are asking to decrease our cost of living here. We are just asking you to give us proper roads because from morning till night, roads play a major role in our lives. Those are the main source which take us from one part to another part.

I really hope you take action on it as soon as possible because it is really needed.

He tried to break my vehicle lock and confiscated vehicle key also.After that he made to me pay 500 RS but paid 480 as I was having only that much.He behaved with me very badly. What is the proof that I am only putting the garbage?? Don't other people have same color cover??. They looted me and took 480 rs which was there in my wallet.
